HOW TO PLAY

Each hand has 4 betting rounds. In each round, everyone still in the hand has to end up with the same amount bet. If nobody bets, everyone checks for free.

  1. PRE-FLOP: you get 2 cards. Two players post the blinds (forced bets of $10 and $20) so there is always something at stake. That is why you need to put in at least $20 (CALL) to see the flop.
  2. FLOP: 3 community cards are dealt. New round: if nobody bets, you can CHECK and stay in without paying.
  3. TURN: the 4th community card. Another betting round.
  4. RIVER: the 5th community card. Last round.
  5. SHOWDOWN: the remaining players show their cards. The best 5-card hand made from your 2 cards and the 5 on the board wins.

CHECK: pass without putting in money (only if nobody has bet). CALL: match what someone else bet. BET / RAISE: bet or raise; it is optional, you are never forced to. FOLD: give up and lose what you already put in. ALL-IN: bet all your chips.

If you run out of chips you can't play until you take a $1,000 loan from the casino. While you are in debt, what you win each hand goes to paying it off first.

HAND RANKINGS

From best to worst. Your hand is the best 5 cards you can make from your 2 cards and the 5 on the board. The gold cards are the ones that make the combination.

1
Royal flushA, K, Q, J and 10 of the same suit. The best possible hand.
A♠K♠Q♠J♠10♠
2
Straight flush5 cards in a row of the same suit.
9♥8♥7♥6♥5♥
3
Four of a kind4 cards of the same rank.
Q♣Q♦Q♥Q♠7♦
4
Full houseThree of a kind and a pair at the same time.
K♥K♦K♠4♣4♥
5
Flush5 cards of the same suit, in any order.
A♦J♦8♦6♦2♦
6
Straight5 cards in a row of any suit. The ace can be high (10-J-Q-K-A) or low (A-2-3-4-5).
10♣9♦8♠7♥6♣
7
Three of a kind3 cards of the same rank.
7♠7♥7♦K♣2♠
8
Two pairTwo different pairs.
J♣J♥5♠5♦A♣
9
Pair2 cards of the same rank.
A♥A♦9♣6♠3♥
10
High cardNone of the above: the highest card counts.
K♠J♦8♣5♥2♠

THINKING ABOUT YOUR HAND

  • The board belongs to everyone. If the pair is on the board, everyone has it: what counts is what your 2 cards add.
  • Same type of hand: the higher one wins (a pair of kings beats a pair of eights). If they are equal, the highest leftover card breaks the tie, the kicker: A-A-K beats A-A-Q.
  • Count your "outs": the cards still to come that improve your hand. With 4 hearts you have 9 hearts left for a flush. Trick: outs × 4 after the flop (or × 2 after the turn) = rough % chance of hitting.
  • Read the board like your opponent: if there are 3 cards of the same suit, someone may have a flush; if they are in a row, a straight. The more possibilities, the more careful you should be.
  • Starting hands matter: high pairs (A-A, K-K, Q-Q) and A-K are very strong; unrelated low cards (offsuit 7-2) almost never win.
  • The best hand doesn't always win: if you bet big and everyone folds, you win without showing your cards. The bots know this too and sometimes bluff.
